t: Jayavarman II began the Angkorian period around 800 CE, and Yasovarman built the city of Yasodharapura around the hill of Phnom Bakheng from 889.
Suryavarman II built Angkor Wat between 1113 and 1150, and after the Cham sack of 1177 Jayavarman VII built the walled city of Angkor Thom and the Bayon over the ruins of the old capital.
Angkor was sacked by Ayutthaya around 1431 and nearly all of it was abandoned in the 15th century, though Angkor Wat remained a Buddhist shrine.
dyk: A study in 2007 using satellite photographs concluded that Angkor had been the largest pre-industrial city in the world by surface area, with an urban sprawl of at least 1,000 square kilometres.
ev: Jayavarman II declares himself universal monarch and god-king
Yasovarman ascends the throne and builds Yasodharapura around Phnom Bakheng
Suryavarman II begins Angkor Wat, which is built between 1113 and 1150
Cham forces sack the capital and kill the reigning king
Jayavarman VII takes the throne and builds Angkor Thom and the Bayon
The Chinese diplomat Zhou Daguan arrives at Angkor
Ayutthaya sacks Angkor and its population moves south to Longvek
The École française d'Extrême-Orient begins the restoration of the site

f.founded: The Angkorian period began around 800 CE with Jayavarman II; the city of Yasodharapura, centred on Phnom Bakheng, was built by Yasovarman, who ascended the throne in 889.
f.where: Amid forests and farmland north of the Great Lake (Tonlé Sap) and south of the Kulen Hills, near the present city of Siem Reap in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia.
f.known: The capital of the Khmer Empire; Angkor Wat, built between 1113 and 1150 by Suryavarman II; the walled city of Angkor Thom and the Bayon of Jayavarman VII; a system of roads, canals and reservoirs; the account of Zhou Daguan in 1296
f.today: Angkor is a group of ruined temples and other monuments in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992 and administered as the Angkor Archaeological Park.
